## Sanity check on channel B

**What the data actually shows (net_contribution = job margin minus channel spend, by quarter):**

Channel B spend has been flat at **$800/quarter** for the last three quarters, and returns have been climbing on that same $800:

| Quarter | B spend | B net contribution | Implied job margin | ROI (margin/spend) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Q4 2025 | $800 | $4,240.82 | $5,040.82 | 6.3x |
| Q1 2026 | $800 | $6,412.16 | $7,212.16 | 9.0x |
| Q2 2026 | $800 | $10,000.00 | $10,800.00 | 13.5x |

For comparison, channel A (spend $1,000/quarter) ran $4,390 → $4,083 → $7,000 net contribution over the same three quarters (ROI roughly 5–8x), and referral (zero spend) threw off $38,080 net contribution in Q2 alone, dwarfing both paid channels.

**The catch:** every one of those three quarters was spent at the *same* $800. There is no quarter in the data where B was ever run at a higher spend, so there's no observed data point for what an extra $800 (taking it to $1,600) actually buys. The quarter-over-quarter growth you're seeing happened with spend held constant, which means it's coming from something other than budget size, better lead quality, conversion, seasonality, and I can't attribute how much of it is spend-elastic versus not. Doubling the channel's budget is not the same experiment as the trend you're extrapolating from.

**Capacity is not the constraint right now:** technician utilization for Q2 2026 shows one tech at 94% and four others under 4% utilized (520 available hours each), so if channel B does convert into more jobs, there's crew slack to absorb it, as long as those idle techs are certified for whatever service lines B's leads book into.

**Recommendation:** the historical ROI on the existing $800 is genuinely strong and getting stronger, that part of your read is right. But treat the extra $800 as a test, not a sure thing, since it's unprecedented spend for this channel. A smaller step first (or splitting the $800 across two quarters) would give you an actual second data point on B's spend curve before you commit the full amount.

ANSWER: Channel B's net contribution has grown from $4,240.82 to $6,412.16 to $10,000.00 over the last three quarters, all at the same flat $800 spend, so that growth is not proven to come from budget size and there's no historical data point at $1,600/quarter to say what the next $800 gets you. Crew capacity has slack to absorb more jobs if channel B does convert, so I'd test the increase in a smaller step rather than doubling it outright.
